entities.name: Prisse Papyrus
entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary:
The Prisse Papyrus is an ancient Egyptian text written on papyrus in abbreviated hieratic script, sometimes referred to as the "oldest book in the world",
named after the French Egyptologist Émile d'Avennes, who purchased the papyrus scroll in Cairo in 1843 claiming it was stolen from excavations he was conducting near Thebes. Prisse later donated 1947 the papyrus to the Bibliothèque nationale de France and published its facsimile at the same time.
